title: Early saxophonists and Sidney and Professor Carrere
summary: The only early sax player he knew was Sidney Carrere; they sort out Sidney and his brother Professor Carrere, who gave Raymond Burke a lesson.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Excuse me, who were some of the other early saxes before you?

Who else played sax in those days? The only one that I knew at that particular time was Sidney Carrere. You heard of Sidney Carrere? Yeah. He was the only one that. He was a big heavy fellow. Was he pretty big?
No, Sidney's a little bitty man.
I'm thinking somebody else. Yeah, he's a little bitty fellow.
Somebody else with a big round face like a- One of his brothers I think is supposed to be Professor.

Oh, that's it. Yeah, they lived out around, around Constance and Dallas somewhere. Raymond Burke once told the clarinetist, you know the white clarinetist, he said he took a lesson or two. From Professor Carrere. Yeah. Yeah.

Well he had a- He made him play on his, blow on his mouthpiece and Raymond got discouraged and quit or something after the first lesson. Just wanted to blow on the mouthpiece without any sax at first, you know. Yeah. He had an embouchure. Well he was a good reed man, Sidney was. But anyway, he was the first man that I saw with a clarinet outside. They had a couple of white boys hands. Yeah. Yeah. He had a little boy. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
